activities.anchor: Yet an arrangement — the absence of a clinic, which could have been otherwise — shortened a life
activities.caption: bet before you read on — is that violence?
activities.name: pcsClinicPredict

config.q: Two patients catch the same treatable pneumonia; one dies where clinics are absent. No one attacked them. Does the field count that as violence?
choices: Yes — if an arrangement that could have been otherwise shortens a life, the framework counts it
Only if someone profits from the arrangement
config.why: Galtung's radicalising move: a country without gunfire can still be violent — and the answer decides the field's entire agenda, from wars and criminals to quiet countries with unequal life expectancy.

activities.anchor: the typology is built precisely to keep those two from being confused
activities.caption: file each feature — positive peace or imposed stability
activities.name: pcsStabilitySort

items.label: order imposed by repression — a violent 'peace'
authoritarian order scoring as negative peace with structural violence intact

config.why: It is nearly the opposite: stability can be imposed by repression, while positive peace is specified by justice and functioning institutions.

activities.anchor: stopping the shooting saves lives now
activities.caption: true or false — the ceasefire overcorrection
activities.name: pcsCeasefireJudge

statements.s: If negative peace is insufficient, ceasefire diplomacy is pointless.
statements.why: The framework says no such thing: stopping the shooting saves lives now and is the precondition for everything else.

statements.s: The framework's claim is about sufficiency, not worth.
statements.why: Negative peace is the necessary first half of a job.

statements.s: Learners who meet Galtung often overcorrect into dismissing ceasefire diplomacy.
statements.why: The documented trap — the collapse comes when the first half is treated as the whole job.

statements.s: A ceasefire that freezes a conflict counts as failure, full stop.
statements.why: It counts as one link delivered — insufficient, genuinely valuable.

activities.anchor: critics note that marking a culture "violent" risks its own kind of prejudice
activities.caption: pair each violence layer with its signature
activities.name: pcsViolenceMatch

config.prompt: Galtung's three layers — pair each with its signature:

pairs.right: an identifiable actor doing identifiable harm — war, assault, murder
harm built into arrangements — excess mortality, no shooter needed
the stories and symbols that make the other two look normal, natural or deserved

config.why: Read as a pyramid: the legitimating layer sits at the base — remove it and the harms above are harder to justify. Specific stories, never cultures as wholes.

activities.anchor: any peace process that never goes below the waterline is a schedule, not a settlement
activities.caption: sequence the iceberg's layers
activities.name: pcsIcebergOrder

config.prompt: Below the waterline, in depth order:
items: behaviour — the fighting, the protest, the breakdown (the visible tip)
contradictions — contested land, excluded groups, economic imbalance
latent conflict — the iceberg underwater, waiting; resolve only the behaviour and it regenerates
config.why: Resolve only the behaviour while attitudes and contradictions persist, and the conflict regenerates — positive peace is a society whose triangle is managed.

activities.anchor: mixing hard data (battle deaths, refugees, homicides, imprisoned populations) with qualitative expert assessments
activities.caption: pair each measure with its method
activities.name: pcsIndexMatch

config.prompt: How a contested field measures itself — pair them:

pairs.right: about 160 countries, 23 indicators across three domains, annually since 2007
eight pillars of institutional conditions, linked to resilience and relapse risk
armed conflicts coded since 1946 — a 'war' needs 1,000 battle-related deaths in a year

config.why: The numbers do not settle the definitional debates — but they expose patterns the definitions must reckon with: the post-1945 shift from interstate war to civil conflict, relapse concentrated where positive peace is thin.

config.root: Three recurring objections, three replies. Walk the defence of the framework.

start.text: Critique one — expansion: 'if violence includes structures, it covers everything and explains nothing.' The reply?

choices.label: The avoidability criterion keeps the concept bounded

decoration.text: The definition does analytical work: avoidable harm that shortens life is not decoration — and whether the extension is wise stays a fair debate.

agency.text: Critique two — agency: 'structural violence names no perpetrator — who is tried?' The reply?

choices.label: Answer with the benefits question: who benefits from the arrangement persisting?

culprit.text: Law wants a defendant; the framework answers politically — coherent, but unsatisfying in courtrooms.

comparability.text: Critique three — comparability: 'how much structural violence equals how much direct violence?' The reply?

choices.label: No exchange rate — the typology clarifies categories, not trade-offs

rate.text: There is no exchange rate to run — which is precisely the third objection's point.

done.text: Held together, the framework earns its keep as a lens — hypothesis generator, not verdict machine.

config.why: Knowing where a definition breaks is part of knowing it — the controversies are part of the toolkit.

activities.anchor: a new well that redrew whose land was worth fighting for
activities.caption: drag between neutral aid and conflict sensitivity
activities.name: pcsAidCompare

before.label: the comfortable assumption
before.text: Aid is neutral — relief, reconstruction contracts and wells sit outside the conflict system.

after.label: the conflict-sensitive view
after.text: Every intervention enters the system and changes it — analyse the dividers and connectors before acting: who is being empowered, whose grievance is being fed, which local rivalry your distribution is about to fund.

config.why: Anderson's 'Do No Harm' crystallises it — positive peace, applied, means designing interventions that connect rather than divide.
